The carbon nanotubes used had a high purity level of 96%.
The carbon nanotubes were used without any functionalization.
The polyester resin was used as the matrix material.
The carbon nanotubes and polyester resin were first mixed with 3% hardener and left to cure for 2 days.
The resulting mixture was then mixed with polyester resin at a 1% loading level.
The saturation magnetization values decreased from 2.58 emu/g for <8 nm particles to 2.13 emu/g for 48-78 nm particles.
The coercivity values decreased from 111.39 Oe for <8 nm particles to 97.39 Oe for 48-78 nm particles.
The minimum reflection loss value of -9.38 dB was observed for the composites with 48-78 nm carbon nanotube particles.
The effective bandwidth for the 48-78 nm composites was determined to be 10.27 GHz.
Improved impedance matching, interfacial scattering, and dielectric and magnetic losses were identified as the key mechanisms behind the outstanding electromagnetic wave absorption performance.

The study introduces an innovative and efficient approach to fabricate a promising electromagnetic absorption material with characteristics such as lightweight, robust absorption capability, and a broad absorption bandwidth.
The results of this research can serve as a guide for future studies on optimizing microwave absorption properties and using these materials in various applications.
The XRD patterns confirmed the dimensional consistency of the received carbon nanotubes at the specified levels.
SEM images showed that the carbon nanotubes had a homogeneous and stable structure.
The Network Analyzer and coaxial line armature were calibrated to perform the microwave absorption measurements.
